clue.text: Callously ditch husband and finally spill the beans knowing …

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of each of the following words in turn

blocks.note: a rut is a channel or furrow in the ground
standard abbreviation for husband
the last letters of spill, the and beans
knowing in the sense of artful or cunning

explanation.surface: Someone coldly dumps their husband and, at last, confesses everything with a knowing look.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to 6 across for the surface only; RUT + H + LES + SLY stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting ruthlessly means acting without pity or compassion, which is what acting callously means.

clue.text: Harry H Corbett and dad joke essentially cause trouble

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so only the central letters of each word are kept
to harry is to harass or pester, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle letter of dad and the middle two of joke

explanation.surface: The actor Harry H Corbett, of the sitcom Steptoe and Son, and a groan-worthy joke stir things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the actor's first name, but it is the anagram signal; Harry H Corbett was a British comic actor, best known as Harold Steptoe.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock the boat is an idiom for upsetting a settled situation, that is, stirring up trouble.

clue.text: See 1
Line with copy on back of novel is part of jacket's design

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for line
to ape is to imitate
the final letter of novel

explanation.surface: A line of text copied onto the back of a novel forms part of its dust-jacket design.
explanation.walkthrough: The jacket suggests a book's dust jacket; the definition means a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded-back flap on the front of a coat, a standard element in how a jacket is styled.

clue.text: Notices drug ring is making a comeback

indicators.note: something making a comeback returns the way it came, so the words are read backwards

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a ring of criminals is a gang
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police notices warn that a drug ring is back in business.
explanation.definitionFit: Signage is the collective term for signs and public notices displayed in a place.

clue.text: A row divides support for chief

indicators.note: something dividing another sits in the middle of it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or chair
taken as written
a row in the sense of a racket or loud noise

explanation.definitionFit: Leading as an adjective means principal or foremost, the same as chief in 'the chief cause'.

clue.text: … audiotape captures scrap

indicators.note: the word captures, so the needed letters are held inside the longer word

blocks.note: sitting in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across, a recording on tape catches a fragment of the confession.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is a tiny amount, from the smallest Greek letter, just as a scrap is a small piece.

clue.text: Grace, say, after about a week in leaderless African country with little chance of success

annotation.answer: ON A WING AND A PRAYER

indicators.note: without a leader means the country's name loses its first letter
after sends the piece it follows in the clue to the end of the answer

blocks.note: on in the sense of concerning
taken as written
standard abbreviation for week
taken as written
Uganda without its first letter
grace is a prayer said before a meal; say marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Someone named Grace has spent about a week in an African country with poor prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace looks like a woman's name, but it is the prayer before a meal, which comes last in the answer because of 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming in on a wing and a prayer is an idiom, from damaged wartime aircraft, for getting by with only hope to rely on.

clue.text: See 7
Maybe Jasper's posh fridge company raised quality

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word means it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Smeg is an upmarket Italian maker of fridges
tone as in the character or quality of something

explanation.surface: Someone called Jasper has a fancy fridge that has improved in quality.
explanation.walkthrough: Jasper looks like a person's name with a possessive; it is the mineral, with 's meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque variety of quartz used in jewellery, so it is an example of a precious or semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Material, having moved last bit back one inch

indicators.text: having moved last bit back one
indicators.note: the final letter is shifted one place towards the front, rearranging the word

blocks.note: crepe is a thin crinkled fabric

explanation.surface: Fabric whose final piece has been shifted back by one inch.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last E of the fabric moves, hopping one place left past the P.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch and to creep both mean to move very slowly and gradually forward.

clue.text: Many here are late heading to Graeme Garden's following party

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
following places the possessive piece after the one named next in the clue

blocks.note: the opening letter of Graeme
a rave is a large dance party
a yard is the American word for a garden; it follows the party

explanation.surface: Many people turn up late to the comedian Graeme Garden's party.
explanation.walkthrough: Graeme Garden is a British comedian, one of The Goodies. Late here means dead, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is where the dead are buried, and the late are those who have died.

clue.text: Peeled globe artichoke regularly cooked with a cabbage

indicators.note: peeling removes the skin, so the outer letters are stripped away
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the word with its outer letters removed
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: a trimmed globe artichoke cooked alongside a cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: Globe artichoke reads as one vegetable, but globe and artichoke are worked separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a cultivar of cabbage grown for its swollen, turnip-like stem.

clue.text: Runner and politician cut corners

blocks.note: a ski is a runner on snow, as on a sledge
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An athlete and a politician both take shortcuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner suggests an athlete; it is a ski, the long blade something glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise by doing less than is needed, which is what cutting corners means.

clue.text: Perhaps stays in institution with man carrying weapon

indicators.note: one who carries something holds it within, so the second word goes inside the first

blocks.note: a foundation is an endowed institution, such as a charity
short for gentleman
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: Someone perhaps remains in an institution with an armed man.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays reads as a verb, but it is the old noun for a corset; perhaps marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays, a corset stiffened with bone, are a classic example of a supporting undergarment.

clue.text: Shock when say, art turns on home study group

indicators.note: something that turns round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the Open University, which teaches by distance learning
e.g., for example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A home study group is shocked when art takes against them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is the UK's distance-learning university; 'on' places it in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a strong feeling of shock and anger, so it can stand for shock as a noun.

clue.text: Discovered with cap gun, somehow misbehaving

indicators.note: dis-covered means its cover is taken off, so the outer letters go and the inside stays
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the word without its outer letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child caught with a toy cap gun has been behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Discovered looks like 'found out'; it means stripped of its cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting up is an informal phrase for behaving badly, especially of children.

clue.text: State of European getting into all-round excellent Australian beer

grog is Australian slang for beer or alcohol

explanation.surface: A European fits right in with a top-quality Australian beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 and GROG are reversed together, then E slips in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is one of the fifty US states, and also a country; either sense matches state.

clue.text: Denied need to control 17 tons

indicators.note: to control something is to have it held in your grip, so it sits within

blocks.note: taken as written
the postal abbreviation for the answer to 17 across
standard abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Someone refuses that a need could manage seventeen tons.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 stands for the answer to 17 across, and the US state's postal code is GA.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a claim is to deny or contradict it, so negated is a past tense of denied.

clue.text: See 14
Rubbish here in south of France — heading north initially, to Belgium if necessary

blocks.note: sud is the French word for south
the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A trip from the south of France north to Belgium, with rubbish to dispose of on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: South of France reads as the Riviera, but it means the French word for south.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustbin is a household container for refuse, so it is where rubbish goes; dustbin is the British word for a trash can.

clue.text: Shot of brownish-grey tree broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the words count by their sound

blocks.note: taupe is a brownish-grey colour, and the oak is a tree

explanation.surface: A shot of a greyish-brown oak shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: A toe poke is a football shot struck with the tip of the boot; shot seems to mean a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe poke is a kind of kick at goal in football, so it is a type of shot.

clue.text: Reported attempt to get engineers under ship

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an attempt is a try
the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps; they go under the first part

explanation.surface: A reported effort to get engineers working below decks on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's corps of Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme is an ancient galley with three banks of oars, so it is a kind of ship.

clue.text: Various people putting spades beneath extra smooth turf

explanation.walkthrough: The S comes first in the clue but goes beneath everything else, at the foot of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and sods is British slang for a miscellaneous assortment of people or things.

clue.text: Stage article about actor who makes a living?

explanation.definitionFit: An apron is the part of a theatre stage that projects forward in front of the curtain.

clue.text: Eject Microsoft product after making copyright one of PowerPoint's biggest features

C as in the copyright symbol
the capital P in PowerPoint, of which there are two
